headline: After a fast plunge to $2,028, Ether bounced and has held above $2,061 five candles running while buyers now outnumber sellers, so a tighter long now pays 2 to 1 or better.

messages.text: Round 2 update: the Judge is right, my first target only paid about the same as my risk. I fixed it. New plan: buy near $2,068 with a closer exit at $2,054 (only $14 risk), so the $2,096 target pays $2 for every $1 risked.

messages.reply_to: Bear: only $0.69 of buy orders for every $1 of sell orders
messages.text: That has flipped. A few minutes later buyers have $1.19 waiting for every $1 of sellers, so the lopsided picture is gone.

messages.reply_to: Bear: That looks like a big panic sell, not a calm dip
messages.text: Agreed it was a panic, and that is my point. In one 5-minute candle price fell from $2,109 to $2,028, then bounced back to $2,066. Panics that get bought back that fast are often the bottom of the move.

messages.reply_to: Bear: But oversold can stay oversold
messages.text: True, so I am not betting on RSI alone. The five candles after the plunge all dipped only to about $2,061 and buyers kept stepping in. That is a small base, like a ball resting on a step above the floor. If it breaks, my exit at $2,054 gets me out.

messages.reply_to: Bear: Big US Ethereum funds lost about $272 million
messages.text: Outflows are real, but news sites disagree ($365M in one, $184M in another), so I will not pretend to know the exact number. Much of today's drop was forced selling of borrowed-money bets (about $449M+ of liquidations, mostly longs), and some big wallets bought. This is a few-hours trade, not a bet on the whole month.

messages.reply_to: Bear: The nearest ceiling... is $2,096. That is only about $27 above us
messages.text: Right, so I shrank my risk to match. Target 1 at $2,096 is $28 up for $14 of risk (2 to 1), and target 2 at $2,113 is $45 up (about 3 to 1).

argument:
Fresh data (13:58 UTC): ETH 2072.66. Since the first snapshot, three things changed in the bull's favour. (1) Order-book bid/ask went from 0.69 to 1.19 (bids $1.44M vs asks $1.21M). Top-100 book depth is volatile, so I treat this as a rebuttal to Bear's 0.69, not a standalone signal. (2) The 13:30 5m candle was a liquidation flush: high 2109.09, low 2028.32, close 2066.12 on 35,566 volume, followed by five candles with lows 2061.16, 2061.11, 2063.32, 2068.09, 2066.66, so the flush low was not retested and a micro-base sits near 2061. (3) Short-term RSI is recovering: 5m 37.5, 15m 31.2; 15m MACD histogram -1.37 versus -1.55 earlier, though the 1h histogram is still negative at -2.68.

Fix to the Judge's flag: the Round 1 plan used a stop at 2022 (about 38 from entry), so target 1 (2096) paid about 0.95:1. The base gives a structural, tighter invalidation: stop 2054 is under the 2061 base lows and about 1.4x the 5m ATR (10.10) away. Entry 2068: risk 14. T1 2096 (session VWAP 2096.13): +28 = 2.0:1. T2 2113 (1h EMA21 2113.72): +45 = 3.2:1. Scale out half at T1 and move the stop to entry.

Admitted weaknesses: every moving-average check on every timeframe remains bearish; the 1h SMA200 is 2248.48; 5m volume has faded to 0.44x average; a retest of 2028 stops this trade out for a 14-point loss. ETF outflow totals conflict across search snippets ($365.2M for Nov 2-6 vs $184.5M), so I accept the direction (outflows) but not any exact figure. Liquidation reports of roughly $449-462M, mostly longs, point to forced selling that is largely spent, and funding is only +0.0025%, so there is no crowded-long overhang.

evidence.claim: Fresh price 2072.66; 5m RSI 37.5, 15m RSI 31.2, 1h RSI 27.3 (5m and 15m up from 34.4 and 28.5 at the first snapshot)
evidence.plain: The speed meter is climbing off the floor on the short charts, so the selling push is easing.

evidence.claim: Order book top 100 bid/ask ratio 1.19 ($1.44M bids vs $1.21M asks), was 0.69
evidence.plain: Buyers now have more waiting orders than sellers: $1.19 of buy orders for every $1 of sell orders. What Bear pointed at has flipped.

evidence.claim: 5m candle 13:30 UTC: high 2109.09, low 2028.32, close 2066.12, volume 35,566 (the previous 5m candles traded about 300-1,500)
evidence.plain: In a few minutes price plunged about $80 and then bounced about $38 off the very bottom. A fast plunge that gets bought back is called a flush.
Price has not gone back toward the day's low. Dips stop around $2,061 and buyers step in.
The first target ($2,096) is the day's average price, about $24 up. A normal 5-minute wiggle is about $10, so a $14 stop sits outside normal noise.
Almost nobody is overpaying to bet on a rise, and fear is high but easing a little. Not a crowded trade.

evidence.claim: News roundup: about $449-462M of ETH liquidations in 24h (about 92% longs); a whale bought 8,773 ETH; BitMine bought another 9,587 ETH; ETF outflow totals differ by source ($365.2M for Nov 2-6 vs $184.5M)
evidence.plain: A lot of the selling was forced (borrowed-money bets wiped out), which ends once they are gone. Some big buyers are still buying. ETF numbers conflict between sites, so I do not lean on them. Search snippets only, pages not opened.
evidence.source: WebSearch results: crypto.news, cryptotimes.io, cryptoticker.io (snippet only)

rebuttals.response: Now 1.19 (bids $1.44M vs asks $1.21M). Depth moves around, so it neither proves nor refutes the trade, but the one-sided picture is gone.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: panic sell, not a calm dip; no base yet
rebuttals.response: The 13:30 candle was a flush (low 2028.32, close 2066.12). Five following candles all held lows of 2061 or higher, a small base that the new stop sits just under.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: oversold can stay oversold in a trend
rebuttals.response: Accepted; the trade does not rest on RSI. It rests on the flush-and-hold structure, with a stop 14 points away that limits the cost of being wrong.
Snippets show conflicting totals ($365.2M vs $184.5M), so the exact size is uncertain. Outflows are a multi-week backdrop; this is a 2-6 hour trade after a forced-selling flush.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: weakest vs BTC since July; $2,000 at risk
rebuttals.response: Headline only. $2,000 is about 3.5% below the price; the stop at 2054 exits well before that, so a $2,000 break costs only the 14-point stop.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: R:R to VWAP about 0.65:1 with stop under 2028
rebuttals.response: Fair for that stop. With the stop moved to just under the 2061 base (2054), R:R to VWAP is 2.0:1 and to the 1h EMA21 is 3.2:1.

plan_plain: Buy around $2,068. If price falls to $2,054 (just under the little floor at $2,061), sell and take a small $14 loss. Take half the profit at $2,096 and move your exit up to your buy price, then aim for $2,113. That is about $2 won for every $1 risked at the first target, and about $3 at the second.
